title: Power lifting and finite generation for PGL invariants
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $r\geq1$, and let $G=\operatorname{PGL}_{r,k}$ be the affine group scheme of invertible $r\times r$ matrices modulo scalar matrices. A rational action of $G$ on a commutative $k$-algebra $E$ means a coaction $\rho:E\to E\otimes_k k[G]$ satisfying the counit and coassociativity identities; put $E^G=\{e:\rho(e)=e\otimes1\}$. For every finitely generated $k$-algebra $E$ with such an action, $E^G$ is finitely generated over $k$. For every surjective equivariant map $u:E\twoheadrightarrow F$ of finitely generated commutative $k$-algebras and every $b\in F^G$, there are $N>0$ and $a\in E^G$ with $u(a)=b^N$. If the algebras are nonnegatively graded, their actions preserve degree, $u$ is graded and $b$ is homogeneous of degree $d$, the lift can be chosen homogeneous of degree $Nd$. These assertions hold in every characteristic.

source.place: Alper, Adequate moduli spaces and geometrically reductive group schemes, arXiv:1005.2398v3, Sections 9.1--9.2 and Theorem 9.7.6 (PGL is geometrically reductive), Theorem 6.3.3 (finite generation). Local PDF WANTED; read online at https://arxiv.org/pdf/1005.2398. Milne Algebraic Groups, Aside 12.58, printed p.250, is a local corroboration for finite generation.

proof.text: By the structure theorem $G=\operatorname{PGL}_{r,k}$ is reductive, including the trivial case $r=1$. Apply the symmetric-power theorem: for every finite-dimensional rational $G$-module $V$ and equivariant surjection $\lambda:V\to k$, some invariant $q\in\operatorname{Sym}^N V$ maps to $1$, with $N>0$. All invariance below is the coaction identity, not merely invariance under $G(k)$.

source.place: Theorem 9.7.5; Lemma 9.2.5 (5-prime); read online, local PDF WANTED; agent-written algebraic details.

proof.text: We first prove power lifting for arbitrary rational $G$-algebras, even without finite-generation assumptions. Let $u:D\twoheadrightarrow D\prime$ and $b\in(D\prime)^G$. If $b=0$, take $a=0,N=1$. Otherwise $M=u^{-1}(kb)$ is a rational submodule: it is the kernel of the equivariant linear map $D\to D\prime/kb$, and tensoring over the field preserves kernels. Choose $e\in M$ with $u(e)=b$, and use the finite-subrepresentation theorem inside $M$ to obtain a finite-dimensional rational $V\subset M$ containing $e$. The map $u|_V$ has the form $v\mapsto\lambda(v)b$ with $\lambda:V\twoheadrightarrow k$ equivariant. Choose $q,N$ as in Step 1. Multiplication gives an equivariant map $\operatorname{Sym}^N V\to D$; its value $a$ on $q$ is invariant and satisfies $u(a)=\operatorname{Sym}^N(\lambda)(q)b^N=b^N$.

source.place: Lemma 9.2.5 (5-prime) implies (3), explicit finite-submodule and multiplication argument; read online, local PDF WANTED; agent-written algebraic details.

proof.text: If $D,D\prime$ are nonnegatively graded with degree-preserving actions and $u$ graded, write the invariant lift from Step 2 as $a=\sum_j a_j$. Projecting $\rho(a)=a\otimes1$ to degree $j$ gives $\rho(a_j)=a_j\otimes1$. If $b$ has degree $d$, projection of $u(a)=b^N$ to degree $Nd$ gives $u(a_{Nd})=b^N$. Thus $a_{Nd}$ is the required homogeneous invariant lift. This includes degree zero and $b=0$.

source.place: Graded refinement of Lemma 9.2.5 (3): componentwise coaction and graded map; read online, local PDF WANTED; agent-written algebraic details.

proof.text: We prove a stronger finiteness assertion by Noetherian induction: for every finitely generated rational $G$-algebra $D$, the ring $R=D^G$ is finitely generated over $k$, and for every finitely generated equivariant $D$-module $M$, its invariants $M^G$ are finite over $R$. Equivariant means a rational coaction compatible with multiplication by $D$. The algebra $D$ is Noetherian, so the maximal condition on ideals permits induction on its $G$-stable ideals, with the assertion assumed for all quotients by nonzero stable ideals. The zero algebra is immediate. Invariants preserve kernels: both kernels and invariants are given by the coaction equations, and tensoring over $k$ is exact. We never assume surjectivity on invariants.

source.place: Theorem 6.3.3, property (star) and Noetherian induction; read online, local PDF WANTED; agent-written algebraic details.

proof.text: First record an implication used in the induction. If $I\subset D$ is stable and $T=(D/I)^G$ is finitely generated over $k$, then every $t\in T$ satisfies $t^N-c=0$ for some $c$ in the image $S$ of $R\to T$, by Step 2. Thus each member of a finite set of $k$-algebra generators of $T$ is integral over $S$. The integral-adjoining theorem shows that $T$ is finite over $S$, hence over $R$. Artin--Tate applied to $k\subset S\subset T$ shows that $S$ is finitely generated over $k$. The zero quotient is allowed.

source.place: Lemma 6.3.1, expressed for invariant quotient rings; Stacks 00IS for Artin--Tate; read online, local PDF WANTED; agent-written algebraic details.

proof.text: Suppose $I,J$ are nonzero stable ideals with $IJ=0$. The induction hypothesis applies to $D/I,D/J$. By Step 5, their invariant rings $R_I,R_J$ are finite over the respective finitely generated image rings $S_I,S_J$ of $R$. Choose lifts to $R$ of finite $k$-algebra generating sets of both $S_I,S_J$, and let $B\subset R$ be generated by these lifts. Then $B$ maps onto both image rings, so $R_I,R_J$ are finite $B$-modules. The ideal $I$ is a finite equivariant $D/J$-module because $D$ is Noetherian; induction therefore makes $I^G$ finite over $R_J$, hence over $B$. Left exactness gives $0\to I^G\to R\to R_I$. Since $B$ is a finitely generated $k$-algebra it is Noetherian; the image in $R_I$ is a finite $B$-module. Choose generators of that image and lift them, then adjoin generators of $I^G$ to obtain finite $B$-module generators of $R$. Hence $R$ is finitely generated over $k$.

source.place: Lemma 6.3.2, first part; explicit two-ideal argument; read online, local PDF WANTED; agent-written algebraic details.

proof.text: Continue in the two-ideal case of Step 6. For a finite equivariant $D$-module $M$, the modules $IM$ and $M/IM$ are finite over $D/J$ and $D/I$, respectively. Induction makes $(IM)^G$ and $(M/IM)^G$ finite over $R_J$ and $R_I$, respectively, and therefore over $R$ by Step 5. In $0\to(IM)^G\to M^G\to(M/IM)^G$, the image is finite because $R$ is Noetherian by Step 6 and the finite-type algebra theorem. Lifting generators of the image and adding generators of the kernel proves $M^G$ finite over $R$. This completes the stronger assertion whenever such $I,J$ exist.

source.place: Lemma 6.3.2, second part; explicit module argument; read online, local PDF WANTED; agent-written algebraic details.

proof.text: If a nonzero invariant $f\in R$ is a zero divisor of $D$, take $I=fD$ and $J=\operatorname{Ann}_D(f)$. Both are nonzero stable ideals, since multiplication by the invariant $f$ is equivariant; their product is zero. Steps 6--7 apply. We may therefore assume that every nonzero element of $R$ is a non-zero-divisor in $D$. If an invariant $f$ is a unit in $D$, its inverse is invariant because $\rho(f^{-1})=\rho(f)^{-1}=f^{-1}\otimes1$. Thus for a nonzero proper ideal $K\subset R$ and $0\ne f\in K$, the ideal $fD$ is proper and nonzero. Moreover $R\cap fD=fR$: if $h=fa$ is invariant, then $(f\otimes1)(\rho(a)-a\otimes1)=0$, and injectivity of multiplication by $f$ remains injective after tensoring over $k$, so $a$ is invariant.

source.place: Theorem 6.3.3, zero-divisor reduction and exactness of invariant multiplication; read online, local PDF WANTED; agent-written algebraic details.

proof.text: For $K,f$ as in Step 8, induction applies to $D/fD$. Step 5 shows that the image of $R$ in $(D/fD)^G$ is finitely generated over $k$. By Step 8 this image is $R/fR$, hence is Noetherian. The ideal $K/fR$ is therefore finitely generated; lift its generators and add $f$ to generate $K$. The zero and unit ideals are generated by the empty set and by $1$. Thus every ideal of $R$ is finitely generated, proving $R$ Noetherian. This also covers the case that $R$ is a field.

source.place: Theorem 6.3.3, proof that the invariant ring is Noetherian; read online, local PDF WANTED; agent-written algebraic details.

proof.text: Step 2 established the power-lifting hypothesis for all rational $G$-algebras, so the invariant-quotient submersiveness theorem applies to $D$. It says that $\operatorname{Spec}D\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is universally submersive. The ring $R$ is Noetherian by Step 9, and $D$ is finitely generated over $k$. The Noetherian-subring finite-type criterion now gives that $R$ is finitely generated over $k$.

source.place: Theorem 6.3.3, application of universal submersiveness and Theorem 6.2.1; read online, local PDF WANTED; agent-written algebraic details.

proof.text: To finish the stronger assertion in the remaining case, let $M$ be a finite equivariant $D$-module and induct on its equivariant quotients, using the maximal condition on $D$-submodules. If $M^G=0$ there is nothing to show. Otherwise choose $0\ne s\in M^G$. Its cyclic submodule $Ds$ is equivariant and isomorphic to $D/L$, where $L=\operatorname{Ann}_D(s)$ is stable. If $L=0$, then $(Ds)^G\simeq R$ is finite; if $L\ne0$, induction on algebra quotients and Step 5 show that $(Ds)^G$ is finite over $R$. The proper module quotient $M/Ds$ has finite invariants by the module induction. Since $R$ is Noetherian, the image of $M^G$ in $(M/Ds)^G$ is finite. Left exactness and lifting generators again prove $M^G$ finite. This closes both inductions, rather than assuming the module assertion during the algebra proof.

source.place: Theorem 6.3.3, last paragraph, module induction; read online, local PDF WANTED; agent-written algebraic details.

proof.text: Apply the completed stronger assertion to $D=E$ to obtain finite generation of $E^G$. Apply Step 2 to the given $u:E\twoheadrightarrow F$ to obtain the positive-power lift, and Step 3 for its homogeneous refinement. The structural and symmetric-power inputs hold over every field, and no averaging, invertibility of a group order, reducedness of the algebras, or restriction on the characteristic entered any step.

source.place: Assembly of the three clauses of the item; read online, local PDF WANTED; agent-written algebraic details.
